standard_prerequisites: Impurities as witnesses that a module is not pure along a point, and the definition of purity along a point in terms of the associated points of the geometric fibres
The etale local ring at a geometric point as the filtered colimit of the rings of etale neighbourhoods, and the limit characterisation of purity that follows from it

Ascent of an impurity along a locally quasi-finite base change, and the fact that a quasi-finite morphism over a strictly henselian base becomes finite after passing to an open and closed neighbourhood
Base change of the relative assassin under a finite morphism, and closedness of the induced map on underlying spaces
core_obligations: Record that the first two formulations are equivalent by the definition of purity along a point

Write the etale local ring as the filtered colimit of the rings of affine etale neighbourhoods, so that the spectrum of the local ring is the limit of those neighbourhoods, and deduce that an impurity over the local ring descends to an impurity over an etale neighbourhood
Observe that an etale morphism is locally quasi-finite, so the third formulation implies the fourth
Assume the fourth formulation and, after shrinking, replace the given impurity by an impurity obtained by locally quasi-finite base change along the local ring

Use that the local ring is strictly henselian to make that quasi-finite morphism finite after passing to an open and closed neighbourhood, track the image of the impurity inside the relative assassin of the pullback, and use finiteness to recognise the closure of that image as the closure of a point, which produces an impurity over the local ring and closes the circle
proof_roadmap: Identify the first two formulations definitionally
Descend an impurity from the local ring to an etale neighbourhood through the limit description
Note that etale implies locally quasi-finite to get the fourth formulation from the third
Go from quasi-finite back to the local ring, making the morphism finite over the strictly henselian base and tracking associated points
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the equivalence of four formulations of purity along a geometric point at source lines 401-421, label lemma-pure-along-X-y, whose proof occupies source lines 423-467. Besides the definitional equivalence of the first two formulations, the proof has two nontrivial directions: it descends an impurity from the spectrum of the etale local ring to an etale neighbourhood by writing that ring as a filtered colimit of the rings of affine etale neighbourhoods and using the limit characterisation of purity, and it ascends an impurity along a locally quasi-finite base change to the local ring, where the strictly henselian hypothesis turns the quasi-finite morphism into a finite one after passing to an open and closed neighbourhood, after which the relative assassin of the pullback and closedness of the map on underlying spaces identify the closure of the image of the impurity with the closure of a point. The counted statement records neither the limit argument nor the strictly henselian finiteness step.
